sources: RotoWire NFL player news, all 32 team feeds (retrieved 2026-08-23)
Sleeper players API: depth chart position and order, injury status and body part, roster status
FantasyPros Expert Consensus rankings: ECR, rank standard deviation and tier
ESPN public fantasy API kona_player_info: PPR draft rank, ADP and season outlook
FantasyCalc current values: dynasty superflex, redraft 1QB and redraft superflex, with 30-day trend
Beat reporters and team official sites quoted within RotoWire items (The Athletic, ESPN, NFL Network, local papers and team sites)

ARI.brief: Jacoby Brissett opens as the starter with Carson Beck (ribs) day-to-day and out of the second preseason game, so the passing game is in a holding pattern behind Marvin Harrison and Trey McBride. The backfield is the bigger fantasy story: Jeremiyah Love suffered a high-ankle sprain in the preseason and needs no surgery, but Arizona is only 'hopeful' for Week 1, and Trey Benson has not reached 11-on-11 work because of a knee issue. Tyler Allgeier is the fallback and could open as the primary back. Guard Chase Bisontis went to IR with an MCL injury, thinning an already unsettled line.

ATL.brief: Tua Tagovailoa has the inside track to start Week 1 under Kevin Stefanski, but Michael Penix was cleared for 11-on-11 work on Aug 22 and the competition is live again, which is the single biggest swing factor for this passing game. Bijan Robinson is the offense's centerpiece and has been held out of preseason action entirely. Drake London and Kyle Pitts are the primary target earners; Zachariah Branch has been the busiest of the depth receivers. Guard Kam Dewberry was carted off Saturday, another hit to the interior line.

BAL.brief: Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry return intact and both were rested through the preseason opener, so nothing has changed at the top. The interior line took a real hit: center Danny Pinter tore his patella tendon in a joint practice and is likely out for the season, pushing Ethan Pocic into the starting job. Zay Flowers and Mark Andrews remain the passing-game hierarchy behind Rashod Bateman, who is facing three charges from a June domestic incident, a situation with roster and availability risk attached. Rookie-level depth pieces Ja'Kobi Lane and Elijah Sarratt have flashed but are not in the Week 1 rotation.

BUF.brief: Josh Allen is healthy and sat out the second preseason game as a precaution. The receiver room is the concern: Keon Coleman is in a walking boot with a sprained right foot/toe, Khalil Shakir missed time with an undisclosed issue, and Skyler Bell has a lower-body injury. DJ Moore, acquired this offseason and now the nominal WR1, tweaked an ankle but returned to team drills and downplayed it. James Cook is the unquestioned lead back with Ray Davis handling change-of-pace and goal-line work in exhibitions. Dalton Kincaid is the starting tight end but played only nine preseason snaps.

CAR.brief: Bryce Young is the starter and has been efficient in limited preseason work. The backfield is a stated committee: Chuba Hubbard is week-to-week with a hamstring but Dave Canales is confident about Week 1, and Jonathon Brooks has started both exhibitions and scored. Tetairoa McMillan is the clear WR1; Xavier Legette is in a boot with an ankle injury from a joint practice and John Metchie has made a case for the WR3 role in his absence. Carolina signed Darren Waller to a one-year deal, immediately complicating a tight end room that already had Tommy Tremble and Ja'Tavion Sanders.

CHI.brief: Caleb Williams is the starter and played one series in the second preseason game. The backfield opened up when Kyle Monangai hyperextended his right knee and was deemed week-to-week, leaving D'Andre Swift as the clear lead back and Salvon Ahmed as the depth piece who has flashed. Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland are the young pass catchers to watch; Loveland made his preseason debut Aug 22 and Cole Kmet remains ahead of nobody in name only. Backup QB Tyson Bagent is week-to-week with a hamstring. Tackles Braxton Jones and Ozzy Trapilo are both back from knee issues.

CIN.brief: Joe Burrow is healthy and was rested for the second preseason game after two sharp drives in the opener. Cincinnati is installing a new offense and Burrow described the fit as coming together late in camp, worth monitoring for early-season pace and efficiency. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are both fully healthy with no camp absences, an unusually clean bill of health for this pair. Chase Brown is the lead back with Samaje Perine in the change-of-pace role. The tight end job is Mike Gesicki's with rookie Jack Endries pushing for a roster spot.

CLE.brief: Deshaun Watson is atop the depth chart but was outplayed by Shedeur Sanders in the second preseason game, and the job is not settled in any meaningful sense. That uncertainty caps the ceiling of every pass catcher here. Quinshon Judkins missed practice time with what Todd Monken called a minor nagging issue and did not play Saturday; he remains the lead back over Dylan Sampson. Cedric Tillman has been sidelined with an undisclosed injury and Isaiah Bond cleared concussion protocol during Saturday's game. Harold Fannin is the starting tight end and one of the more interesting young pieces on the roster.

DAL.brief: Dak Prescott is healthy and has not played in the preseason. Javonte Williams sits atop the depth chart but Jaydon Blue has been the most productive back in exhibitions, running 15 times for 75 yards Saturday after clearing a shoulder issue, so the split is not settled. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens headline a deep receiver group; Jake Ferguson is the tight end and has been held out. Brandon Aubrey remains one of the few genuinely set-and-forget kickers in fantasy. Backup Joe Milton threw for 179 yards and three total touchdowns Saturday, which matters only for trade chatter.

DEN.brief: Bo Nix looked sharp in his preseason debut and is entrenched under Sean Payton. The backfield is a genuine three-way rotation: J.K. Dobbins is listed first, RJ Harvey scored a receiving touchdown Friday, and Jonah Coleman is trending toward a real role per beat reporting. That committee suppresses everyone's floor. Jaylen Waddle, new to the offense, returned from a leg issue and hit a 35-yard gain in his team debut. Courtland Sutton, Troy Franklin and Evan Engram round out the pass catchers, with Marvin Mims working through an undisclosed issue.

DET.brief: Jared Goff was rested Saturday and the top of the offense is unchanged, with Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown as the anchors. The concern is tight end: Sam LaPorta is dealing with a hip injury and Dan Campbell would not commit to him being available for Week 1 against the Saints. Jameson Williams has been managing a minor shoulder issue but returned to team drills. Detroit's backfield depth behind Gibbs and Isiah Pacheco is unsettled after a run of injuries to Kye Robichaux, Jacob Saylors and Jabari Small. Guard Michael Niese left Saturday's game on crutches.

GB.brief: Jordan Love is healthy and played into the second preseason game under Matt LaFleur. Josh Jacobs (groin) returned to practice but sat out Friday's game; his Week 1 availability looks fine but the missed camp reps are worth noting. The bigger flag is Tucker Kraft, who tore an ACL last season and has only just been cleared for 11-on-11 work; Kraft himself said he expects a snap count 'probably until halfway through the season,' which is a direct hit to his early-season ceiling. Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and Jayden Reed form the receiver rotation. MarShawn Lloyd has handled preseason starts behind Jacobs.

HOU.brief: The receiver room was reshaped when Jayden Higgins tore an ACL in an Aug 18 practice and went to IR on Aug 21, ending his season. That vacates a projected starting role opposite Nico Collins and pushes Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel (hamstring/finger, ramping up) and newly signed veterans Zay Jones and Sterling Shepard into the competition. C.J. Stroud was rested for the second preseason game after a plan change. David Montgomery leads the backfield with Woody Marks, who scored Thursday, as the complement. Dalton Schultz remains the starting tight end.

IND.brief: Daniel Jones is listed as the starter with Anthony Richardson behind him, and Richardson is expected to remain on the roster in 2026. Indianapolis added Keenan Allen on a one-year deal on Aug 17, which crowds a slot role Josh Downs already occupies. Alec Pierce has missed all of training camp with an ankle injury and remains on PUP, a serious problem for anyone drafting him at his current price. Tyler Warren strained a groin in a joint practice and is expected to miss about a week, with his Week 1 status not in danger. Jonathan Taylor is the workhorse and untouched by any of this.

JAX.brief: Trevor Lawrence is healthy and sat out the preseason under Liam Coen. The receiver picture is muddled: Jakobi Meyers jammed his right hand and is wearing a brace, Parker Washington has been day-to-day with an undisclosed issue but returned to walkthroughs Sunday, and Travis Hunter did not play Friday and remains third on the slot depth chart, which is the single biggest gap between his draft cost and his projected role. Brian Thomas is the clear WR1. Bhayshul Tuten leads the backfield with LeQuint Allen out for the rest of camp with a soft-tissue injury. The line has been reworked: Patrick Mekari had back surgery and Daniel Faalele was acquired from the Giants.

KC.brief: Patrick Mahomes is recovering from an ACL injury and said Aug 22 he is 'extremely confident' he will play Week 1 against Denver on Sept 14, but he has not played in the preseason and Justin Fields has been taking the first-team reps. That is real risk for every Chiefs pass catcher through September. Kenneth Walker is the new lead back with Emari Demercado listed second and Emmett Johnson and Brashard Smith behind. Xavier Worthy is working back from a shoulder injury and has been limited to 7-on-7. Rashee Rice and Travis Kelce are the established target earners. Guard Trey Smith is trending toward Week 1 availability.

LV.brief: Klint Kubiak has declined to name a Week 1 starter between Kirk Cousins and rookie Fernando Mendoza, and Mendoza started the second preseason game and threw a pick-six. Sleeper lists Mendoza first. That unresolved competition is a drag on the whole passing game. Ashton Jeanty is the workhorse back and was rested Thursday; Mike Washington has been the standout backup with long runs in both exhibitions. Brock Bowers played one snap in the opener and remains the offense's best player. Jack Bech, Tre Tucker and Malik Benson are competing for perimeter snaps, with Benson earning first-team reps.

LAC.brief: Justin Herbert is healthy and played a single series Thursday. The offensive line took a major blow when center Tyler Biadasz suffered ACL damage and additional knee injuries in an Aug 18 practice; he is out indefinitely with the team hoping for a late-season return. That is a real drag on the run game and on Herbert's pocket. Omarion Hampton is the lead back over Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell. Ladd McConkey is the primary receiver; Quentin Johnston has been in and out with a lower-body issue and Tre' Harris has been managing an undisclosed problem. The tight end room is a three-way split between Oronde Gadsden, David Njoku and Charlie Kolar.

LAR.brief: Matthew Stafford is healthy and has not played in the preseason. Puka Nacua has been sidelined for weeks with a groin/psoas issue and missed the Aug 20 joint practice after Sean McVay initially expected him back; that timeline has slipped more than once and is the key thing to track here. Davante Adams was also rested. Kyren Williams leads a backfield where Jarquez Hunter has produced in exhibitions. Terrance Ferguson has seen an expanded route tree this summer and is the starting tight end, with Davis Allen (quad) nearing a return. The defense has been dominant in exhibitions, shutting out New Orleans 34-0.

MIA.brief: The quarterback situation is the story: Malik Willis is listed first with Quinn Ewers week-to-week with a groin injury under Jeff Hafley. That caps the passing game's realistic ceiling. De'Von Achane is the offense's clear focal point and did not play Saturday. The backfield behind him is unsettled after Ollie Gordon exited Saturday's game with an undisclosed injury; Jaylen Wright is the other option. The receiver room is thin and young, led by Jalen Tolbert and Malik Washington, with Chris Bell close to full clearance from an ACL rehab. Greg Dulcich is the starting tight end.

MIN.brief: Kyler Murray won the starting job over J.J. McCarthy, and Justin Jefferson has been building rapport with him at practice. McCarthy said he wants to remain in Minnesota and was 'a little hobbled' in Saturday's game. Kevin O'Connell's offense still runs through Jefferson, with Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings behind him and T.J. Hockenson at tight end. The backfield is a Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones split with neither getting more than three carries in the preseason opener. Tackle Caleb Tiernan hurt an ankle Aug 15.

NE.brief: Drake Maye is the starter and looked sharp in camp, including a deep connection with A.J. Brown, who is now the WR1 here and was held out of the preseason opener. The backfield is a stated near-even split between TreVeyon Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson per The Athletic's Chad Graff, which caps both. Romeo Doubs has been the standout at camp practices and Kyle Williams flashed a long touchdown Saturday. Hunter Henry is the tight end. Kicker Andy Borregales is volatile, missing three of five in the opener before going 1-for-1 with three PATs Saturday. Two guards, Ben Brown and Andrew Rupcich, are out for extended time.

NO.brief: Tyler Shough is listed as the starter ahead of Spencer Rattler and Zach Wilson, and Wilson started the second preseason game, so the job is not settled and the passing game is hard to trust. Alvin Kamara sprained an MCL in an Aug 18 joint practice with Dallas and is out at least a month, which hands Travis Etienne a heavier early-season workload; beat reporting explicitly flags Etienne as the beneficiary. Devin Neal (hamstring) and Kendre Miller are the depth. Chris Olave leads the receivers; Jordyn Tyson is listed Doubtful. New Orleans was shut out 34-0 by the Rams.

NYG.brief: Jaxson Dart is the starter under John Harbaugh and was rested Saturday. Malik Nabers is working back from an ACL tear, has logged 11-on-11 reps in a red non-contact jersey, and Harbaugh said he must take contact before being cleared for Week 1 against Dallas; that is the highest-leverage medical situation on the roster. The backfield got crowded when the Giants signed Najee Harris (Achilles) on Aug 18, joining Cam Skattebo, Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary. Tracy has fumbled in consecutive exhibitions and Singletary outplayed him Saturday. JuJu Smith-Schuster was released. Isaiah Likely is the starting tight end.

NYJ.brief: Geno Smith is the starter and was perfect on his lone drive Friday under Aaron Glenn. Breece Hall will be sidelined two to three weeks with a groin injury, which puts Braelon Allen in the lead role to open camp and possibly into the season; Isaiah Davis (knee) also sat Friday. Garrett Wilson is the unquestioned WR1 and returned from an illness. Adonai Mitchell is the perimeter complement. Tight end Kenyon Sadiq is working back from a hernia and Glenn said he remains on track for Week 1, with Mason Taylor available if not.

PHI.brief: Jalen Hurts and Saquon Barkley are healthy and untouched by the preseason churn. The receiver room is banged up: DeVonta Smith has been limited with a hamstring, Makai Lemon has missed extended time with his own hamstring and did not play Saturday, Elijah Moore has a neck injury from a joint practice, and Johnny Wilson reverted to IR with a knee. That thins the group behind Smith considerably and raises Dallas Goedert's target share. Tank Bigsby returned from a toe issue and is the primary backup to Barkley. Jake Elliott remains the kicker.

PIT.brief: Aaron Rodgers is the starter under Mike McCarthy and was rested for the second preseason game. Both starting receivers have been limited: DK Metcalf missed practice time with an undisclosed issue but says he is fine for Week 1, and Michael Pittman has a minor hamstring problem that has kept him out since mid-August. The backfield is a Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle split, with both getting five carries Friday, and Kaleb Johnson is reportedly in danger of being cut despite leading the team in preseason rushing. Pat Freiermuth is the tight end. Pittsburgh's defense remains a strong streaming unit.

SEA.brief: Sam Darnold is the starter under Mike Macdonald and did not play in the preseason opener. The backfield is unusual: Zach Charbonnet remains on the active/PUP list working back from an ACL injury and Jadarian Price is listed first, with Emanuel Wilson (hamstring) behind. Anyone drafting Charbonnet at his consensus rank is paying for a player who has not practiced. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is the clear WR1, with Rashid Shaheed and Cooper Kupp behind him; Jake Bobo went to IR with a serious knee injury and Tory Horton has been working through an undisclosed issue. AJ Barner is the starting tight end.

SF.brief: Brock Purdy is healthy and looked sharp Thursday. George Kittle is on PUP working back from an Achilles injury but visited Dr. ElAttrache on Aug 20, remains ahead of schedule, and has a chance to play Week 1 against the Rams; his consensus rank still bakes in meaningful risk. Christian McCaffrey did not play Thursday with an undisclosed issue and has been managed carefully all summer. The receiver room is new: Mike Evans (quad) returned to 11-on-11 Saturday, Christian Kirk (calf) is still working on a side field, and Deebo Samuel made his preseason debut. De'Zhaun Stribling has impressed but is day-to-day with a shoulder.

TB.brief: Baker Mayfield is healthy and played two series Saturday under Todd Bowles. The receiver room is the problem: Emeka Egbuka is 'day-to-day, week-to-week' with a toe injury and Bowles was non-committal about the Sept 13 opener against Cincinnati, and Jalen McMillan has been in and out with a knee. Chris Godwin is the healthy constant in the slot. Bucky Irving made his preseason debut with three carries and is the lead back, with newly added Kenny Gainwell drawing public praise from Mayfield. Cade Otton missed practice with an undisclosed issue. Tristan Wirfs practiced for the first time in camp on Aug 17.

TEN.brief: Cam Ward is the starter under Robert Saleh. The backfield is a Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears split, with Pollard back from a brief absence and Nicholas Singleton leading the team in preseason carries; Tennessee added D'Ernest Johnson for depth. Calvin Ridley and Wan'Dale Robinson are the primary receivers, with rookie Carnell Tate missing practice time after a hard hit and general stiffness. Gunnar Helm is the starting tight end after Jaren Kanak tore a pectoral and was placed on IR for the season. Backup QB Mitchell Trubisky has a biceps issue.

WAS.brief: Jayden Daniels made his preseason debut Saturday and was rusty in one series, but he is healthy and the offense runs through him. The backfield is a mess: Jacory Croskey-Merritt is listed first but sat Saturday, Rachaad White has missed practice with a hamstring and will not play, and Jeremy McNichols has a quad injury, leaving Kaytron Allen as the only healthy back getting volume. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs both played Saturday, with Diggs making his preseason debut. Chig Okonkwo is the starting tight end. Center Nick Allegretti has a calf issue.

4984.outlook: The consensus QB1 across all seven sources with a perfect or near-perfect rank at every one, and the market agrees at 1 overall in both superflex configs. His value is built on rushing volume that no other quarterback matches, which makes him close to matchup-proof in six-point passing TD formats like DU & Friends. He is fully healthy and was rested for the second preseason game. In two-QB and superflex leagues he is the most expensive asset in fantasy football and correctly so.
4984.watch: A rushing-volume decline, since his floor is built on legs rather than arm.

4881.outlook: QB2 by consensus with tight agreement across sources, and both a healthy Lamar and a healthy Derrick Henry returning intact means the offense should look like it did last year. His dynasty value has slipped to 3rd in superflex while his redraft value held at 2nd, which is an age signal at 29 rather than a performance concern. Rushing production gives him the same matchup-proof profile as Allen. The one structural change is on the interior line, where center Danny Pinter's torn patella tendon pushed Ethan Pocic into the starting job.
4881.watch: Interior line play after losing Pinter for the season.

11564.outlook: Third year in a row of consensus movement upward, now QB3 at age 23 with a 47.3 ESPN ADP. He was sharp in camp, including a deep connection with A.J. Brown, who is the clear WR1 in New England now. His superflex dynasty value sits second overall behind only Allen but dropped 358 points over the last 30 days, a sign the market had gotten ahead of itself. The backfield is a near-even Henderson and Stevenson split, which means fewer goal-line carries taken away from him than a workhorse team would.
11564.watch: Whether the A.J. Brown connection holds up once real coverage arrives.

6770.outlook: QB4 by consensus and effectively tied with Maye on average rank. He is fully healthy for the first time in a while and so are Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, an unusually clean bill of health for this trio. Cincinnati is installing a new offense and Burrow described the fit as only coming together late in camp, which is the one real caution on an early-season start. His redraft value dropped 291 points in 30 days. Four-point passing TD formats like PFFP dampen his edge relative to the rushing quarterbacks above him.
6770.watch: How quickly the new offense clicks in September.

11566.outlook: QB5 with tight source agreement and a 50.8 ADP. He made his preseason debut Saturday and was rusty on one series, which means nothing. The rushing floor is what buys him this rank. Washington's backfield is genuinely broken right now with Croskey-Merritt, Rachaad White and Jeremy McNichols all banged up, which if anything pushes more goal-line work his way early. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs both played Saturday and are healthy.
11566.watch: Whether the vacant backfield turns into extra rushing touchdowns for him.

6904.outlook: QB6 with the tightest source agreement of anyone in this range. His fantasy value has always been about the tush push and goal-line rushing rather than passing volume, which makes him more valuable in four-point passing TD leagues than his raw yardage suggests. Philadelphia's receiver room is banged up, with DeVonta Smith limited by a hamstring, Makai Lemon missing extended time and Elijah Moore dealing with a neck injury, which likely means more Dallas Goedert and more designed runs. Saquon Barkley is healthy and untouched.
6904.watch: Whether the thin receiver room forces more short-area passing.

3294.outlook: QB7 by consensus but the market is warmer than that, with a 251-point 30-day gain in redraft. He is healthy and has not played in the preseason. Dallas has one of the deepest receiver groups in the league with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, and Jake Ferguson at tight end. At 33 with a long injury history his dynasty value has fallen to 16th in superflex even as redraft holds at 10th. In six-point passing TD leagues he is a strong QB1 value at an 85.9 ADP.
3294.watch: His durability, which has dictated his last several seasons.

6797.outlook: QB8 with the tightest source agreement in the position group and a 107.7 ADP that makes him one of the better values on the board. The problem is the offensive line: center Tyler Biadasz suffered ACL damage and additional knee injuries and is out indefinitely, which puts real pressure on the pocket. Ladd McConkey is the primary receiver, with Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris both managing injuries. Omarion Hampton is the lead back. Herbert's floor is high and his ceiling is capped by the same thing it always has been, a run-first Harbaugh offense.
6797.watch: Whether the line holds up without Biadasz.

7523.outlook: QB9 with strong source agreement and a 93.6 ADP. He is healthy and was rested through the preseason under Liam Coen. Brian Thomas is the clear WR1 and the offense's best weapon; the rest of the receiver room is muddled, with Jakobi Meyers wearing a hand brace and Travis Hunter buried third on the slot depth chart. Bhayshul Tuten leads a backfield that lost LeQuint Allen for the rest of camp. The line was reworked after Patrick Mekari's back surgery and the Daniel Faalele trade.
7523.watch: Whether Coen's system unlocks more than the last regime did.

11560.outlook: QB10 by consensus but the market ranks him QB6 in redraft and QB4 in superflex dynasty, one of the widest expert-versus-market gaps at the position. He is 24 with rushing upside and now has Colston Loveland and Rome Odunze developing around him. The backfield opened up when Kyle Monangai hyperextended a knee, leaving D'Andre Swift as the lead back. In six-point passing TD dynasty formats he is a buy relative to his consensus rank; in redraft the 92.3 ADP is fair.
11560.watch: Whether the Odunze and Loveland pairing produces this year or next.

12508.outlook: QB11 with tight source agreement in his second year and a 76.5 ADP that is more aggressive than his consensus rank. The market gained 216 points on him in 30 days in redraft. The big variable is Malik Nabers, who is working back from an ACL tear, has taken 11-on-11 reps in a non-contact jersey, and must take contact before being cleared for Week 1. Dart's ceiling is largely a Nabers question. The backfield behind him got crowded with the Najee Harris signing.
12508.watch: Nabers clearing contact and being available Week 1.

8183.outlook: QB12 with the tightest agreement among sources at the position and a 103.8 ADP. He looked sharp in his preseason cameo. The supporting cast is almost entirely new: Mike Evans is working back from a quad, Christian Kirk is still on a side field with a calf, and Deebo Samuel just made his preseason debut. George Kittle is on PUP with an Achilles injury but has a chance to play Week 1. Christian McCaffrey has been managed carefully all summer. Purdy's production has always tracked the health of the people around him.
8183.watch: Kittle's Achilles and whether McCaffrey holds up.

421.outlook: QB13 at 38 years old with a 80.2 ADP that the market has been chasing, up 266 points in 30 days in redraft. He is healthy and has not played in the preseason. The bigger question is Puka Nacua, who has been sidelined for weeks with a groin and psoas issue and whose return timeline has slipped more than once. Davante Adams gives him a second real target. Superflex dynasty value has fallen to 23rd, which is correct for his age.
421.watch: Nacua's groin, which has slipped multiple return timelines.

3163.outlook: QB14 by consensus with a 137.9 ADP that makes him one of the cheapest set-and-forget starters in redraft. Detroit's offense is intact at the top with Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown. The complication is Sam LaPorta's hip, which Dan Campbell would not guarantee for Week 1, and Jameson Williams working through a minor shoulder issue. Goff's fantasy value is entirely volume and efficiency in a good offense, with no rushing floor, so he is more valuable in six-point passing TD leagues than four-point.
3163.watch: LaPorta's hip, which removes a red-zone target if it lingers.

4046.outlook: QB15 by consensus but the market has him QB11 in redraft and QB9 in superflex dynasty, and both numbers are falling, down 163 and 478 points in 30 days. He is recovering from an ACL injury, has not played in the preseason, and said Aug 22 he is extremely confident about Week 1 against Denver on Sept 14. Justin Fields has been taking first-team reps. Xavier Worthy is also working back from a shoulder injury. This is the highest-variance quarterback on the board: the rank assumes a healthy Mahomes and the medical picture does not fully support that yet.
4046.watch: Whether he actually practices in full before Week 1.

11563.outlook: QB16 by consensus with a 88.1 ADP, and one of the tighter source agreements at the position. He looked sharp in his preseason debut under Sean Payton. The receiver room added Jaylen Waddle, who hit a 35-yard gain in his team debut after working back from a leg issue, alongside Courtland Sutton, Troy Franklin and Evan Engram. The three-way backfield of Dobbins, Harvey and Coleman means Denver is not going to lean on any one runner, which supports pass volume. His superflex dynasty value is 11th and rising.
11563.watch: Whether Waddle becomes the target hog this offense has lacked.

5849.outlook: QB17 by consensus at a 147.0 ADP after winning the Minnesota job over J.J. McCarthy. He has been building rapport with Justin Jefferson at practice, which is the single best thing that could have happened to his fantasy value. Kevin O'Connell's offense is a good landing spot and Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson give him real depth of targets. His rushing floor keeps him startable in six-point leagues. Redraft value is down 75 points in 30 days but superflex dynasty is up 264.
5849.watch: How quickly the Jefferson connection produces in real games.

12545.outlook: QB18 by consensus and listed atop the New Orleans depth chart, but Zach Wilson started the second preseason game and Spencer Rattler is also in the mix, so the job is not settled in any real sense. That uncertainty is why he sits here despite starter-level opportunity. Chris Olave leads the receivers and Travis Etienne inherits a heavier workload with Alvin Kamara out at least a month with an MCL sprain. New Orleans was shut out 34-0 by the Rams in the second exhibition, which is not encouraging for the offense as a whole.
12545.watch: Whether he actually holds the job through September.

4892.outlook: QB19 with a 148.5 ADP and healthy after playing two series Saturday. His fantasy value depends heavily on a receiver room that is currently compromised: Emeka Egbuka is day-to-day to week-to-week with a toe injury that Todd Bowles would not commit on for the Sept 13 opener, and Jalen McMillan has been in and out with a knee. Chris Godwin is the healthy constant. Bucky Irving is the lead back and Kenny Gainwell drew public praise from Mayfield. Redraft value is down 89 points in 30 days.
4892.watch: Egbuka's toe and whether he is ready for Week 1.

6804.outlook: QB20 by consensus at a 158.9 ADP, which undersells a healthy quarterback in a good offense. He was solid in his preseason start under Matt LaFleur. The catch is Tucker Kraft, who said he expects a snap count until roughly midseason coming off an ACL tear, removing Love's best red-zone target early. Josh Jacobs missed camp time with a groin but should be fine for Week 1. Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and Jayden Reed form a receiver rotation that spreads targets thin. Superflex dynasty value is 15th.
6804.watch: Whether the receiver committee ever consolidates into a true WR1.

8161.outlook: QB21 by consensus, which reflects opportunity rather than skill. He is listed atop the Miami depth chart with Quinn Ewers week-to-week with a groin injury, so the job is his for now under Jeff Hafley. The supporting cast is thin: De'Von Achane is the offense's focal point and the receiver room is young and led by Jalen Tolbert and Malik Washington. His redraft market value is 26th at the position, well below his consensus rank, and that gap is the honest read. Only a streaming option in six-point passing TD leagues.
8161.watch: Ewers' groin and whether Miami changes quarterbacks in September.

9758.outlook: QB22 by consensus at a 165.6 ADP, and both his redraft and superflex dynasty values fell sharply in the last 30 days, down 102 and 363. The reason is the receiver room: Jayden Higgins tore an ACL on Aug 18 and went to IR, removing a projected starter opposite Nico Collins. Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel and newly signed veterans Zay Jones and Sterling Shepard are competing to fill that role. Stroud was rested for the second preseason game after a plan change. Collins is still an elite target but the depth behind him is unproven.
9758.watch: Who wins the WR2 job now that Higgins is out for the year.

4943.outlook: QB23 by consensus and the starter in Seattle under Mike Macdonald, though he did not play in the preseason opener. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is a genuine WR1 and Rashid Shaheed and Cooper Kupp give him volume. The backfield is unusual, with Zach Charbonnet still on PUP from an ACL injury and Jadarian Price listed first, which likely means more pass attempts early. Jake Bobo went to IR with a serious knee injury. A streamer in six-point leagues, not a weekly starter.
4943.watch: Whether Smith-Njigba's target share pushes his passing volume up.

5870.outlook: QB24 by consensus and listed as Indianapolis's starter ahead of Anthony Richardson, who is expected to remain on the roster. His source spread is the widest of any starter at 2.97 standard deviation, meaning the experts genuinely disagree about whether he holds the job. The Colts added Keenan Allen on a one-year deal, crowding Josh Downs's slot role, and Alec Pierce has missed all of camp on PUP with an ankle. Jonathan Taylor's workload caps pass volume. Streaming only.
5870.watch: Whether Richardson takes the job back at any point.

3257.outlook: QB25 by consensus and the Arizona starter only because Carson Beck is day-to-day with a rib injury. He was held out of the second preseason game. Marvin Harrison and Trey McBride are real weapons, which is the entire case for him, but Brissett has never supported fantasy production at a startable level. The backfield is a mess with Jeremiyah Love recovering from a high-ankle sprain and Trey Benson not yet in 11-on-11 work. Not a fantasy asset outside deep two-QB leagues.
3257.watch: Beck's ribs, which would end this job as soon as he is healthy.

12522.outlook: QB26 by consensus in his second season as Tennessee's starter under Robert Saleh. His superflex dynasty value is 18th, far above his redraft rank, which is the market pricing in age and job security rather than 2026 production. Calvin Ridley and Wan'Dale Robinson are the primary receivers with rookie Carnell Tate missing practice after a hard hit. Gunnar Helm is the tight end after Jaren Kanak's season-ending torn pectoral. Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears split the backfield. A dynasty hold, not a redraft start.
12522.watch: Whether Carnell Tate emerges as a real target.

9228.outlook: QB27 by consensus with a 168.8 ADP and a redraft value down 162 points in 30 days, though superflex dynasty rose 106. He has been efficient in limited preseason work. Tetairoa McMillan is a legitimate WR1; the room behind him thinned when Xavier Legette went into a boot with an ankle injury, with John Metchie stepping up. The backfield is a stated Hubbard and Brooks committee. Carolina also signed Darren Waller, which gives Young a red-zone target he has not had.
9228.watch: Whether Waller becomes a real red-zone outlet.

96.outlook: QB28 by consensus at 42 years old, rested through the second preseason game under Mike McCarthy. Both starting receivers have been limited: DK Metcalf missed practice with an undisclosed issue but says he is fine for Week 1, and Michael Pittman has a minor hamstring that has kept him out since mid-August. The backfield is a Warren and Dowdle split. His superflex dynasty value at 38th is the honest read on where this is heading. A matchup-based streamer at best.
96.watch: Whether Metcalf and Pittman are both healthy in September.

1373.outlook: QB29 by consensus and the Jets starter, perfect on his lone preseason drive under Aaron Glenn. Garrett Wilson is a genuine WR1 and returned from illness. Breece Hall is out two to three weeks with a groin injury, which puts Braelon Allen in the lead role and probably raises early pass volume. Tight end Kenyon Sadiq is working back from a hernia but is on track for Week 1. Smith has the tightest source agreement of anyone in this tier at 1.02 standard deviation. A deep-league streamer.
1373.watch: Garrett Wilson's target share with Hall sidelined.

6768.outlook: QB30 by consensus and nominally Atlanta's starter with the inside track per Jeremy Fowler, but Michael Penix was cleared for 11-on-11 work on Aug 22 and this is a live competition again. Tagovailoa sat out the second preseason game. Drake London and Kyle Pitts are real targets and Bijan Robinson anchors the offense, so whoever wins this job has fantasy relevance. Redraft value fell 52 points in 30 days as the Penix news landed. Do not start him until the job is settled.
6768.watch: Whether Penix takes the job outright in the final preseason weeks.

4017.outlook: QB31 by consensus and atop the Cleveland depth chart, but he completed five of 12 for 36 yards with an interception Saturday and was outplayed by Shedeur Sanders. This job is not settled and the uncertainty caps every Browns pass catcher. Harold Fannin is the most interesting piece in this offense and Quinshon Judkins leads the backfield. There is no fantasy case for starting Watson in any format, and the roster case is thin too.
4017.watch: Whether Cleveland makes the change to Sanders before Week 1.

13269.outlook: QB32 by consensus as a rookie, listed first on Sleeper's depth chart but with Klint Kubiak explicitly declining to name a Week 1 starter over Kirk Cousins. He started the second preseason game and threw a pick-six. His superflex dynasty value at 14th is dramatically above his redraft rank at 29th, which is exactly right: he is a dynasty asset, not a 2026 starter. Ashton Jeanty is the offense's engine and Brock Bowers is its best player, so the job carries real fantasy weight if he wins it. Relevant to Bobby's two superflex dynasty leagues as a stash.
13269.watch: Whether Kubiak names him the Week 1 starter.

1166.outlook: QB33 by consensus with only three sources ranking him, reflecting how uncertain his role is. Kubiak refused to name him the starter after the second preseason game, which is telling for a 38-year-old veteran on a team that drafted Mendoza. If he wins the job he has Ashton Jeanty, Brock Bowers and a young receiver room, which is enough for streaming value in six-point leagues. If he does not, he has none.

12524.outlook: QB34 by consensus but the market moved hard on him, up 238 points in 30 days, after he completed nine of 11 for 74 yards and a touchdown Saturday and clearly outplayed Deshaun Watson. He is listed second on the depth chart. His source spread of 3.49 standard deviation is the widest at the position, meaning the experts have not caught up to the preseason. In superflex dynasty this is a cheap buy on a quarterback who may take the job in September.
12524.watch: Whether Cleveland names him the starter before Week 1.

11559.outlook: QB35 by consensus but cleared for 11-on-11 drills on Aug 22 after a knee/ACL rehab, and set to return to team work Monday. Kevin Stefanski had limited him to 7-on-7 through mid-August, so this is a real step. Tua Tagovailoa has the inside track per reporting, but Penix now has a live path to the job with Drake London, Kyle Pitts and Bijan Robinson around him. His value dropped 305 points in 30 days before the clearance news, which makes this a buy-low window in superflex dynasty.
11559.watch: Whether the knee holds up through full-contact team work.

11565.outlook: QB36 by consensus after losing the Minnesota job to Kyler Murray. He said he wants to remain with the Vikings and was described as a little hobbled in Saturday's game with an undisclosed issue. He has no 2026 fantasy value as a backup, but at 23 with a starting-caliber pedigree he retains superflex dynasty value at 32nd. A stash in Bobby's two dynasty leagues, nothing more.
11565.watch: Whether he is traded before the season or gets the job back.

9221.outlook: The consensus RB1 and the 1.5 ADP, first at six of seven sources with the tightest spread of any player on the board. He is the overall 1 in FantasyCalc's redraft market and gained 681 points in 30 days, the largest move of any top-tier back. Detroit's offense is intact at the top and Isiah Pacheco is the complementary back, not a threat to his workload. In full PPR his receiving work is what separates him from Bijan Robinson. He is the 1.01 in any of Bobby's redraft leagues.
9221.watch: Detroit's backfield split if Pacheco's health improves.

9509.outlook: Consensus RB2 at a 2.5 ADP with near-universal agreement. He has been held out of preseason action entirely, which is precaution rather than injury. The Atlanta offense is stable around him regardless of whether Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix wins the quarterback job, since his value is volume-driven and not quarterback-dependent. Brian Robinson is the change-of-pace back. His redraft value is essentially flat over 30 days while dynasty slipped slightly, which is normal for a 24-year-old at the top of the board.
9509.watch: Whether the quarterback competition suppresses red-zone efficiency.

6813.outlook: Consensus RB3 with a 7.8 ADP and a true workhorse role that none of the Indianapolis roster churn touches. The Keenan Allen signing and Alec Pierce's PUP status affect the passing game, not him. His redraft value is fourth at the position and flat, while his dynasty value rose 250 points, which is unusual for a 27-year-old and suggests the market is comfortable with his workload holding. Daniel Jones under center caps the offense's ceiling but raises Taylor's carry share.
6813.watch: Whether the Colts' passing game forces more negative game scripts.

4034.outlook: Consensus RB4 at a 7.1 ADP but carrying the widest source disagreement of any back in the top 10 at 2.05 standard deviation, and he did not play Thursday with an undisclosed issue. Sleeper lists him Questionable. At 30 with his injury history, that combination is the definition of a high-risk RB1. The market disagrees with the caution, ranking him RB3 in redraft and up 302 points in 30 days. San Francisco has managed him carefully all summer, which is either good process or a warning sign.
4034.watch: Whether he practices in full before Week 1.

9226.outlook: Consensus RB5 at a 12.0 ADP and the unambiguous focal point of the Miami offense. He did not play Saturday, which is standard for a starter at this point. The concern is the quarterback: Malik Willis is listed first with Quinn Ewers week-to-week on a groin, which caps offensive efficiency but arguably raises Achane's target share since checkdowns become the offense. In full PPR that receiving volume is exactly what you want. His dynasty value rose 399 points in 30 days.
9226.watch: Whether Miami's quarterback play collapses the red-zone opportunities.

8138.outlook: Consensus RB6 at a 12.6 ADP, tied with Achane on average rank, and his redraft value rose 531 points in 30 days, one of the biggest moves at the position. He is the unquestioned lead back in Buffalo with Ray Davis handling change-of-pace and goal-line work in exhibitions. Josh Allen taking rushing touchdowns near the goal line is the structural cap on his ceiling and always has been. Buffalo's receiver room is banged up, which points toward more run volume early.
8138.watch: How many goal-line carries Ray Davis takes.

9224.outlook: Consensus RB7 at a 23.1 ADP and the biggest riser in the entire market, up 918 points in redraft over 30 days. He is the lead back in an offense with a healthy Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, which is about as good a situation as exists. Samaje Perine handles change-of-pace work. Cincinnati is installing a new offense that Burrow said only came together late in camp, which is the one genuine caution. At his ADP he is the clearest value among top-12 backs.
9224.watch: Whether Perine's role grows in the new scheme.

12527.outlook: Consensus RB8 at a 16.1 ADP but the market is cooling fast, down 493 points in redraft and 411 in dynasty over 30 days. The reason is the quarterback: Klint Kubiak has declined to name a Week 1 starter between Kirk Cousins and rookie Fernando Mendoza, and an unsettled passing game means stacked boxes. Jeanty is the workhorse and was rested Thursday. Mike Washington has been the standout backup with long runs in both exhibitions, which is worth watching but not yet a threat.
12527.watch: Who starts at quarterback, since it determines box counts.

4866.outlook: Consensus RB9 at a 15.9 ADP with his redraft value down 336 points in 30 days, an age-29 signal more than anything else. He is healthy and untouched by the Philadelphia injury churn. The receiver room around him is thin with DeVonta Smith limited by a hamstring, Makai Lemon out and Elijah Moore dealing with a neck injury, which points toward more run volume and more Barkley. Tank Bigsby is back from a toe issue as the primary backup. Jalen Hurts still takes the goal-line carries.
4866.watch: Whether Hurts' short-yardage rushing eats his touchdown equity.

12507.outlook: Consensus RB10 at a 26.9 ADP in his second season and the lead back over Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell. The real problem is the offensive line: center Tyler Biadasz suffered ACL damage and additional knee injuries and is out indefinitely, which directly hits interior run blocking. That is likely why his redraft value fell 337 points in 30 days. His dynasty value is sixth at the position, well above redraft, which reflects age. Jim Harbaugh's offense is run-first, so the volume is there.
12507.watch: How the interior line holds up without Biadasz.

3198.outlook: Consensus RB11 at a 19.3 ADP and 32 years old, with the market moving up 282 points in redraft over 30 days. He and Lamar Jackson return intact and both were rested through the preseason opener. The interior line lost center Danny Pinter to a torn patella tendon, replaced by Ethan Pocic, which is a mild negative for a between-the-tackles runner. Justice Hill handles passing downs, which caps his PPR ceiling in a full-PPR league. His dynasty value at 21st is the honest age read.
3198.watch: Interior line play with Pocic at center.

8151.outlook: Consensus RB12 at a 22.6 ADP after moving to Kansas City, with redraft value up 478 points in 30 days. He logged his first touches as a Chief Saturday. The situation is complicated by Patrick Mahomes' ACL recovery, since Justin Fields has been taking first-team reps and Mahomes has not played. Emari Demercado is listed second and Emmett Johnson and Brashard Smith are behind. Walker has the lead role in a good offense, which is the whole case.
8151.watch: Whether Mahomes is actually available Week 1.

8150.outlook: Consensus RB13 at a 42.8 ADP with redraft value up 466 points in 30 days, and one of the tighter source agreements at the position. He leads a Rams backfield where Jarquez Hunter has produced in exhibitions, including a 68-yard, one-touchdown game Saturday. Blake Corum is also in the mix. Williams' fantasy value has always been volume rather than efficiency, so the committee chatter matters. Puka Nacua's extended groin absence points toward more run volume early.
8150.watch: Whether Jarquez Hunter's preseason production earns him real carries.

5850.outlook: Consensus RB14 and dealing with a groin injury that kept him out of Friday's preseason game, though he returned to practice on Aug 18. Sleeper lists him Questionable. The missed camp reps are the concern more than the injury itself. Green Bay's offense is solid with Jordan Love healthy, though Tucker Kraft is on a snap count until roughly midseason. MarShawn Lloyd has handled preseason starts and scored a receiving touchdown, which is the depth to watch. Redraft value is down 96 points.
5850.watch: Whether the groin lingers into the regular season.

7543.outlook: Consensus RB15 at a 45.5 ADP with redraft value up 500 points in 30 days, and the reason is specific: Alvin Kamara sprained an MCL on Aug 18 and is out at least a month, with beat reporting explicitly naming Etienne as the beneficiary. That is a real early-season workload bump in a full-PPR league. The caveat is the New Orleans offense itself, which was shut out 34-0 by the Rams and has an unsettled quarterback job between Tyler Shough, Spencer Rattler and Zach Wilson. Devin Neal (hamstring) and Kendre Miller are the depth.
7543.watch: Kamara's return date, which ends the window.

13287.outlook: Consensus RB16 but this is the sharpest expert-versus-market disagreement at the position: he has a 21.3 ADP and his redraft value fell 956 points in 30 days, the single largest drop in the market. He suffered a high-ankle sprain in the Aug 13 preseason game, needs no surgery, and Arizona is only hopeful for Week 1. Tyler Allgeier could open as the primary back and Trey Benson has not reached 11-on-11 work with a knee issue. High-ankle sprains routinely take longer than teams project. His superflex dynasty value at 4th is the age premium.
13287.watch: Whether he practices in full before Week 1.

7588.outlook: Consensus RB17 at a 36.6 ADP with redraft value up 660 points in 30 days, one of the larger gains at the position. He sits atop the Dallas depth chart but Jaydon Blue has been the most productive back in exhibitions, running 15 times for 75 yards Saturday after clearing a shoulder issue. That split is not settled. Dallas has a healthy Dak Prescott and one of the deepest receiver groups in the league, which means favorable game scripts and plenty of scoring opportunities. Malik Davis is also in the mix.
7588.watch: Whether Jaydon Blue's preseason production earns him the lead role.

8155.outlook: Consensus RB18 but carrying a 3.12 standard deviation, the widest disagreement among any top-20 back, and for good reason: he is out two to three weeks with a groin injury. Sleeper lists the issue as a thigh. That timeline puts Week 1 in real doubt and hands Braelon Allen the lead role to open the season. Geno Smith and Garrett Wilson give the offense some competence. At a 32.8 ADP you are paying a healthy price for a back who may miss September.
8155.watch: Whether he is back for Week 1 or Braelon Allen keeps the job.

12481.outlook: Consensus RB19 with redraft value up 491 points in 30 days despite the backfield getting more crowded. He is listed first on Sleeper's depth chart ahead of Tyrone Tracy and newly signed Najee Harris. Tracy has fumbled in consecutive exhibitions and Devin Singletary outplayed him Saturday, so Skattebo's competition is unimpressive even if the numbers are many. Jaxson Dart is the quarterback and Malik Nabers' ACL recovery is the offense's biggest variable. Note the name: earlier versions of this file had him listed twice as Cam and Cameron.
12481.watch: Whether Najee Harris' Achilles rehab lets him take goal-line work.

6790.outlook: Consensus RB20 at a 66.6 ADP with redraft value up 455 points in 30 days, and the reason is specific: Kyle Monangai hyperextended his right knee and is week-to-week, leaving Swift as the clear lead back. Caleb Williams is the quarterback and the offense has young talent in Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland. Salvon Ahmed has flashed in exhibitions with a 49-yard touchdown catch. Swift's receiving work makes him more valuable in full PPR than his rushing profile suggests.
6790.watch: Monangai's knee and how quickly he returns.

12512.outlook: Consensus RB21 at a 55.0 ADP but redraft value is down 382 points in 30 days. He missed multiple practices with an undisclosed issue that Todd Monken called a little something nagging, and did not play Saturday. Sleeper lists him Questionable. He remains the lead back over Dylan Sampson. The larger problem is the offense: Deshaun Watson was outplayed by Shedeur Sanders and the quarterback job is unsettled, which caps scoring opportunity for everyone. His dynasty value at 13th reflects his age.
12512.watch: Whether the nagging injury is actually minor.

11584.outlook: Consensus RB22 at a 54.8 ADP and the largest faller in the redraft market at this tier, down 841 points in 30 days. He made his preseason debut Saturday with three carries and is the lead back. The market move is probably about Kenny Gainwell, whom Baker Mayfield publicly described as overwhelming talent, plus a receiver room compromised by Emeka Egbuka's toe injury and Jalen McMillan's knee. Tampa Bay's offense functions but the touch split is the live question.
11584.watch: How much of the backfield Kenny Gainwell takes.

12490.outlook: Consensus RB23 at a 74.8 ADP with redraft value up 519 points in 30 days, and he leads the Jacksonville backfield after LeQuint Allen was ruled out for the rest of camp with a soft-tissue injury. His 2.62 source standard deviation is wide, meaning the experts have not settled on him. Trevor Lawrence is healthy under Liam Coen and Brian Thomas is a legitimate WR1, which supports favorable scripts. The offensive line was reworked after Patrick Mekari's back surgery.
12490.watch: Whether the lead role survives once Jacksonville is fully healthy.

5892.outlook: Consensus RB24 at a 71.7 ADP with redraft value up 246 points in 30 days. He leads the Houston backfield with Woody Marks, who scored Thursday, as the complement. He did not play in the second preseason game. The Houston offense lost Jayden Higgins to a season-ending ACL tear, which thins the passing game and probably points toward more run volume. At 29 his dynasty value has slipped to 26th, but his 2026 role is secure and his ADP is reasonable.
5892.watch: Whether Woody Marks takes over the passing-down work.

13286.outlook: Consensus RB25 at a 78.4 ADP and listed first on Seattle's depth chart, which is the entire case for him. Zach Charbonnet remains on the active/PUP list working back from an ACL injury and Emanuel Wilson has a hamstring, so Price has an unobstructed path to the lead role by default. He was a full participant on Aug 17 after a lower-body issue. Sam Darnold is the quarterback and Jaxon Smith-Njigba is a real WR1. His dynasty value at 17th is well above his redraft rank, reflecting his age at 22.
13286.watch: Charbonnet's PUP status and when he is activated.

12529.outlook: Consensus RB26 at a 78.6 ADP, and The Athletic's Chad Graff explicitly projects a near-even split with Rhamondre Stevenson, which is the cap on his ceiling. He is listed first on the depth chart. Drake Maye is a legitimate quarterback and A.J. Brown gives New England a real WR1, so the offense should score. His dynasty value at 16th is well above his redraft rank at 24th, which is the market pricing in the fact that this split resolves in his favor eventually.
12529.watch: Whether the 50-50 split becomes a lead role.

7611.outlook: Consensus RB28 at a 86.9 ADP and the other half of the New England split, with a 2.97 source standard deviation reflecting real disagreement about how it breaks. He is listed second behind TreVeyon Henderson. At 28 his dynasty value at 34th is correctly low. If the split really is 50-50 in a functional Drake Maye offense, both backs are startable in deeper formats, but neither has a weekly RB2 floor.
7611.watch: Whether the split tilts toward Henderson as the season goes.

8228.outlook: Consensus RB29 at a 100.8 ADP with the tightest source agreement of any running back on the board at 0.47 standard deviation, which is unusual. He and Rico Dowdle each carried five times in the second preseason game, confirming a true split. Kaleb Johnson led the team in preseason rushing but is reportedly in danger of being cut, which does not clarify anything. Aaron Rodgers is the quarterback and both starting receivers have been limited. Warren's pass-catching role is what holds his full-PPR value.
8228.watch: Whether the Dowdle split holds all season.

7021.outlook: Consensus RB30 at a 106.0 ADP and the other half of the Pittsburgh split, five carries to Warren's five on Friday. His redraft value is down 136 points in 30 days. He is listed second on the depth chart. At 28 with no clear path to a lead role, he is a bench stash rather than a starter, though if Warren misses time the workload would be substantial in a run-heavy Mike McCarthy offense.
7021.watch: A Warren injury, which would give him a real workload.

11583.outlook: Consensus RB31 at a 119.4 ADP but with a 3.81 source standard deviation, the widest of any back in the top 40, meaning some experts see a starter and others see a backup. He started both preseason games and scored Friday while Chuba Hubbard nursed a hamstring. Beat reporting describes a Hubbard and Brooks committee for the season. Bryce Young is the quarterback and Tetairoa McMillan is a real WR1. At his ADP this is the cheapest path to a potential lead back on this board.
11583.watch: Whether Hubbard's hamstring keeps him limited into September.

6806.outlook: Consensus RB32 at a 118.7 ADP and listed first in Denver, but this is a genuine three-way rotation with RJ Harvey and Jonah Coleman, and beat reporting says Coleman is trending toward a real role. He did not play Friday. Sean Payton's offenses have historically split backfields, which is why his value keeps sliding, down 114 points in 30 days. Bo Nix looked sharp in his debut and the addition of Jaylen Waddle raises the offense's ceiling, but the touch split makes Dobbins hard to start.
6806.watch: Whether the three-way rotation ever consolidates.

7567.outlook: Consensus RB33 with redraft value up 259 points in 30 days after Baker Mayfield publicly said he has been overwhelmed by Gainwell's talent. He rushed once in his Tampa Bay debut. He is listed second behind Bucky Irving, and Irving's 841-point market drop suggests the market thinks Gainwell takes a meaningful share. In full PPR his receiving profile is the part that matters. A speculative bench add rather than a starter.
7567.watch: Whether the praise translates into passing-down snaps.

7594.outlook: Consensus RB34 at a 121.7 ADP but with a 4.88 source standard deviation, the single widest disagreement of any player in this file, and redraft value down 625 points in 30 days. He is week-to-week with a hamstring though Dave Canales expressed confidence about Week 1. Sleeper lists him Questionable and still first on the depth chart. Jonathon Brooks started both exhibitions in his place and scored. Beat reporting frames this as a committee regardless of health.
7594.watch: Whether the hamstring costs him the Week 1 lead role.

12534.outlook: Consensus RB35 at a 128.5 ADP after hyperextending his right knee on Aug 16; he is week-to-week and Jeremy Fowler reported multiple weeks. Sleeper lists him Questionable and second on the depth chart behind D'Andre Swift. His redraft value fell 198 points in 30 days. He was the trendy Chicago backfield pick before the injury and Swift has taken the lead role by default. A stash rather than a Week 1 starter.
12534.watch: Whether the knee lets him back before Swift locks down the job.

12533.outlook: Consensus RB36 and listed first on Washington's depth chart, with both redraft and dynasty values rising, up 181 and 277 points in 30 days. He sat out Saturday with an undisclosed issue and Sleeper lists him Questionable. The Washington backfield is genuinely broken: Rachaad White has a hamstring, Jeremy McNichols has a quad, and Kaytron Allen was the only healthy back getting volume Saturday. Jayden Daniels' rushing takes goal-line work, which is the cap. Whoever emerges healthy here has real volume.
12533.watch: Whether his undisclosed issue is minor and he opens as the lead back.

11586.outlook: Consensus RB37 at a 138.2 ADP with one of the tightest source agreements at the position, 0.87 standard deviation, meaning the experts see him the same way: a clear backup. He is listed second behind Kyren Williams, with Jarquez Hunter also producing in exhibitions. Matthew Stafford's offense scores, so the handcuff value is real, but he needs a Williams injury to matter. His dynasty value at 30th is above his redraft rank.

12489.outlook: Consensus RB38 at a 139.5 ADP with redraft value up 215 points in 30 days. He scored a receiving touchdown Friday and is listed second in a three-way Denver rotation with J.K. Dobbins and Jonah Coleman. His receiving usage in exhibitions is the most interesting thing about him in a full-PPR league. Sean Payton splits backfields, which caps everyone here, but Harvey has looked like the passing-down option.
12489.watch: Whether he consolidates the passing-down role.

8408.outlook: Consensus RB39 at a 142.2 ADP and listed first in Minnesota, splitting with Aaron Jones. He carried three times in the preseason opener. Kyler Murray won the quarterback job and has been building rapport with Justin Jefferson, which should improve the offense. Mason is the bigger back and likely the goal-line option, which is where his value comes from in a committee. His dynasty value rose 177 points.
8408.watch: Whether the Aaron Jones split narrows in his favor.

8136.outlook: Consensus RB40 at a 135.9 ADP with a 3.00 source standard deviation reflecting real disagreement. He has been out for days with a hamstring, was limited to JUGS work off to the side on Aug 20, and will not play in the preseason. Sleeper lists him Questionable and second on the depth chart behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt. The Washington backfield is wide open because everyone in it is hurt, which is both his opportunity and his problem. His dynasty value fell 189 points.
8136.watch: Whether the hamstring clears in time to compete for the lead role.

4199.outlook: Consensus RB41 at a 134.0 ADP and 31 years old, splitting the Minnesota backfield with Jordan Mason. He played one series in the preseason opener. His redraft value is down 214 points and his dynasty value down 134, both correct for his age and role. Kyler Murray's arrival should help the offense overall. In full PPR his pass-catching keeps him marginally relevant, but he is a bench piece.
4199.watch: Whether he retains the passing-down role over Mason.

10219.outlook: Consensus RB42 and listed second in Jacksonville behind Bhayshul Tuten. LeQuint Allen is out for the rest of camp with a soft-tissue injury, which moves Rodriguez up the depth chart by default. Trevor Lawrence is healthy under Liam Coen. This is pure handcuff value with no standalone case at present.

9753.outlook: Consensus RB43 but flagged: he is on the active/PUP list working back from an ACL injury and has not practiced, yet six sources still rank him inside the top 45. Jadarian Price is listed first in Seattle and Emanuel Wilson has a hamstring. His redraft value fell 143 points. Anyone taking him at his consensus rank is paying for a player who has not been on the field, and PUP status means he could miss the start of the season entirely. That gap between rank and availability is exactly the kind of thing worth catching before a draft.
9753.watch: Whether he is activated off PUP before Week 1.

12474.outlook: Consensus RB44 at a 150.8 ADP after rushing four times for 37 yards and a touchdown Thursday. He is listed second behind David Montgomery in Houston. The Jayden Higgins ACL tear thins the passing game and likely pushes Houston toward more run volume, which helps both backs. Marks has looked like the more explosive option. A speculative bench add with genuine handcuff value.
12474.watch: Whether Houston shifts more passing-down work to him.

9508.outlook: Consensus RB45 at a 161.7 ADP with a 3.24 source standard deviation. He was efficient in the preseason opener with 35 yards on four carries and is listed second behind Tony Pollard in Tennessee. Cam Ward is the quarterback in his second season under Robert Saleh. Nicholas Singleton led the team in preseason carries, which muddies the picture behind Pollard. Bench depth only.
9508.watch: Whether Nicholas Singleton passes him on the depth chart.

8132.outlook: Consensus RB46 at a 165.8 ADP but with a genuine path to opening as Arizona's primary back: Adam Schefter reported that Jeremiyah Love's high-ankle sprain opens the opportunity, and Trey Benson has not reached 11-on-11 work with a knee issue. His dynasty value rose 170 points. At this ADP he is one of the better late-round contingency bets on the board, particularly in redraft leagues where Love is going in the second round.
8132.watch: Love's ankle and whether he is ready for Week 1.

12469.outlook: Consensus RB47 at a 170.9 ADP and listed second behind Quinshon Judkins, who has missed practice with an undisclosed issue. At 21 his dynasty value at 48th is well above his redraft rank. The Cleveland offense is the problem, with an unsettled quarterback job between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders capping scoring opportunity. Handcuff value with dynasty upside.
12469.watch: Whether Judkins' nagging injury opens a real role.
